references.text: Moses was commanded to gather the elders of Israel, which shows the same pattern of conveying God's message through leaders.
Moses and Aaron gathered all the elders of Israel and presented the Lord's words to them, the same structure for conveying God's message.
Moses came and told the people all the Lord's words and all the laws, parallel to how he conveyed God's commands.
Moses commanded that the elders be gathered to speak the Lord's words to them, the same pattern for conveying through elders.
The Lord commanded Moses to gather seventy of Israel's elders, showing the elders' role as intermediaries between God and the people.
Paul called together the elders of the church in Ephesus to give them God's message, a similar pattern with elders receiving and conveying God's word.
Both verses illustrate Moses' role as the gatherer of elders to convey the Lord's words, but with different theological emphasis: the introduction of the law versus sharing the prophetic spirit.
Both verses emphasize Moses' total obedience by repeating that he did exactly as the Lord had commanded him.
The connection shows the transition from Moses alone as the messenger to a collaboration between Moses and the elders in laying God's message upon the people.
Both verses use the same structure where Moses gathers the assembly to present the Lord's commands, first for the law and later for the organization of worship.
The verses describe two sides of the same action: Moses' approach to the elders (v.7) and his descent to convey the message further to the people (v.25).
Both verses show how Moses' obedience leads to the assembly gathering to receive or carry out the Lord's commands.
Both verses confirm that Moses' conveying is identical with the Lord's command, whether it concerns the law on Mount Sinai or laws about vows in the wilderness.
Both verses emphasize the same theological principle that Moses carries out the Lord's will exactly as given, from conveying words to practical execution.
